# Retrom public Arcade smoke fixtures

This directory contains deterministic, project-owned MAME 2003, MAME 2003 Plus, FBNeo, FBA2012 CPS1, and FBA2012 CPS2 test programs. They are built entirely from the adjacent Python source and contain no bytes from Pac-Man, PuckMan, 1941, Super Puzzle Fighter II, their BIOSes, or any other third-party game.

Both fixtures deliberately target the public memory map and file layout of the cores' `pacman` drivers. The generated Z80 program fills video and color RAM, reads the active-low P1/P2 ports at `$5000`/`$5040`, and maps independent input counters plus a frame counter to three fixed video RAM areas. The FBNeo addresses and bit assignments are audited against the manifest-bound source commit [`c8c70ba4858458c44b7200b88a29ebbb48c9bb23`](https://github.com/EmulatorJS/FBNeo/blob/c8c70ba4858458c44b7200b88a29ebbb48c9bb23/src/burn/drv/pre90s/d_pacman.cpp); compatibility is still proven by the locked wasm product run. The MAME 2003 resources are split across:

- `pacman.zip`: the four test program ROMs;
- `puckman.zip`: generated character, sprite, palette, lookup, and silent sound data used as a Parent archive;
- `retrombios.zip`: a generated BIOS-role archive used to verify Retrom and EmulatorJS dependency delivery; the MAME driver does not execute this test BIOS;
- `mame2003-smoke.xml`: a small DAT that locks the generated names, sizes, CRC32 values, SHA-1 values, Parent relation, and BIOS/base relation.

The `fbneo/` directory contains the equivalent FBNeo split set and Logiqx DAT. Its Child owns four program and two graphics entries, while its Parent owns the four PROM entries that the FBNeo driver actually loads through the merge relation. FBNeo requires the driver-locked names, sizes, and CRC32 values, so `build.py` solves four generator-controlled bytes in each generated payload to match those public driver CRC32 values. The DAT and fixture tests additionally lock the complete generated bytes with SHA-1 and SHA-256; matching a CRC32 does not imply that any third-party ROM bytes are present.

The generated `retrombios.zip` is identical in both fixture sets. It only verifies Retrom's BIOS/base dependency resolution, snapshot, bundle, and delivery contracts; neither target driver executes it.

`mame2003_plus/` contains an independent copy of the same generated ROM members and DAT for the MAME 2003 Plus acceptance catalog. Its ZIP archives carry a deterministic project-owned archive comment, making their payload identity distinct from MAME 2003 while preserving every driver-visible member byte and CRC. This lets both core-scoped import and validation paths run in one clean database without weakening Retrom's content deduplication rules. `fbalpha2012_cps1/1941.zip` and `fbalpha2012_cps2/spf2xjd.zip` are complete project-authored sets for the cores' public `1941` and Phoenix `spf2xjd` driver layouts. `driver-layouts.json` binds their exact source commit, production DAT digest, entry order, sizes, CRC32 values, load rules, and generator-owned CRC patch windows. The associated test DATs additionally record the actual SHA-1/SHA-256 of every project-authored payload. The pinned CPS2 loader force-opens the `spf2t` zip-name parent before scanning the clone entries, so the test DAT preserves `cloneof`/`romof=spf2t` and the fixture includes a deterministic `spf2t.zip` containing only `retrom-parent.marker`. This project-owned marker is not a game ROM and is not executed by the driver.

The CPS 68000 program initializes deterministic work-RAM counters, samples both active-low player ports, and advances an independent progress counter; the sound CPUs run initialized silent loops. CRC32 compatibility is solved only in non-executed/non-displayed patch windows. Matching the public driver CRCs does not imply any third-party bytes are present.

Run `python3 build.py` to regenerate the files or `python3 build.py --check` to verify the checked-in bytes. The fixture is licensed under the adjacent MIT license.
